Closing - root cause identified: this was not an OpenCode bug. The issue was caused by the `oh-my-openagent` plugin (formerly oh-my-opencode) renaming agent identifiers from lowercase `sisyphus` to capitalized `Sisyphus` after an upgrade. Historical session todos stored the old lowercase agent name, and the Todo Continuation hook attempted to resume with the stale name, triggering `Agent not found` → `UnknownError`. Resolved by clearing historical session data. Filed upstream: https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent — sorry for the noise!

the ephemeral approach is exactly right. we tried persistent team state early on and the recovery logic alone was more code than the actual orchestration.

one thing worth adding to the team tool spec: a timeout per task. different tasks have wildly different completion times, and without per-task timeouts, a single stuck agent blocks the entire Promise.all. we use a watchdog that checks for tool activity (not just process liveness) since an agent can be alive but spinning in circles.

for the inter-agent messaging bus, keep it strictly unidirectional (producer posts, consumers poll). we tried bidirectional agent-to-agent messaging and it immediately degenerated into ACK loops where agents just kept acknowledging each other instead of doing work. the parent collects results, the children never talk to siblings directly.

the depends array for ordering is clean. one edge case: circular dependencies in the DAG. worth adding a cycle check before dispatch rather than discovering it at runtime when two tasks deadlock waiting on each other.

the fork-by-default model with a coordinator is elegant. the Unix process analogy (fork then exec, discard parent context if irrelevant) maps well to how agent sessions actually work.

from running this pattern in production: the coordinator should be deterministic code, not an LLM. we tried LLM-based task decomposition and the coordinator would sometimes create phantom dependencies or reassign tasks mid-flight. the LLM does the actual coding work, but the scheduling and dispatch should be pure code with a simple state machine (pending, claimed, running, done, failed).

for context management on fork, the simple heuristic that works: pass the coordinator's plan summary (not the full conversation) plus the specific task prompt. the subagent almost never needs the parent's full conversation, and injecting it wastes tokens and confuses the model about what it is supposed to focus on.

one thing to add: a session slug that is both human-readable and stable. "fix-auth-middleware-34a" is searchable and debuggable. random UUIDs are not. Claude Code started doing this and it makes a real difference when you are managing 5+ concurrent agents.

I confirmed opencode’s azure-cognitive-services provider is building the wrong host. The bundled code hardcodes https://${AZURE_COGNITIVE_SERVICES_RESOURCE_NAME}.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai, which makes it try .../openai/v1/responses.

My working endpoint is:
https://<resource-name>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview

So the bug is twofold:

- wrong host suffix for Cognitive Services
- wrong request shape for this surface, because it forces the Azure OpenAI-style /v1/responses flow

Suggested fix:

- add an explicit endpoint override via env var for azure-cognitive-services
- preserve AZURE_COGNITIVE_SERVICES_RESOURCE_NAME only for backward compatibility
- let this provider call .../openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview directly instead of forcing /v1/responses
